chunk_findings.detail: When `output.status_fix_tasks_in_headline` is true, the new suffix says only “fix tasks included” and omits the abandoned count. For example, with 15 live tasks (5 normal + 5 fix + 5 abandoned), 8 done among the live/fix tasks, and `abandoned=5`, the line becomes `Progress: tasks 8/15 ... · live tasks, fix tasks included`; the 5 abandoned tasks are excluded from the task denominator but are not disclosed, so the operator cannot reconcile the Progress line with status JSON or STATUS.md totals. The false branch explicitly discloses abandoned tasks, so the true branch should also disclose them (or include them); otherwise the change leaves the exact kind of unexplained total mismatch it is meant to fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/progress_line.py:_progress

chunk_findings.detail: The added `status_completed_shown` row states that `0` “lists all” completions, but the existing `allow_full` row in the same output-caps table states that setting `allow_full=false` “stops 0 lifting a cap.” Given `allow_full=false` and `status_completed_shown=0`, the documentation gives contradictory behavior: the new row promises an uncapped `Completed` list while the general cap contract says a zero cap must not lift. This makes the new knob’s contract unreliable, which is exactly the kind of ambiguity this change is supposed to eliminate.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/output-caps.md:25

chunk_findings.detail: The new expected STATUS.md by-state line is arithmetically wrong for the fixture: it asserts the body contains `2 done + 1 running + 0 review + 0 not started + 0 abandoned = 7`, but those bucket counts sum to `3`, not `7`. The original assertion for the same fixture had `4 open` tasks, so this expected line either drops those four tasks from the displayed buckets while still claiming the total is `7`, or it will fail once the export correctly puts them into a bucket and sums to the total. That directly contradicts the change's stated invariant that every bucket sums to the reported total.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_docs_a.py:331

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert "= 4" in out` does not verify that the reconciled total is exactly four; it is a plain substring check. Given a status output containing any occurrence of `= 4` followed by more characters, such as `total tasks = 40` or an unrelated `bug count = 41`, the test still passes even though the headline does not reconcile to four task records. The same weak check is repeated at line 77, so the test does not reliably tie the printed buckets to the total.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_status_task_count_labels.py:65

chunk_findings.detail: After completing `T2`, the test checks only that the new status contains `"2 of 2 live tasks done"` and never rechecks the reconciled total. If the post-completion status regresses to `2 of 2 live tasks done (1 abandoned and 1 fix tasks listed separately) = 2`, the assertion still passes, so a bug where the total drops from the four records to the live pair after completion would not be caught.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_status_task_count_labels.py:83

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture creates tasks directly in the event log with a phase parent but without the required dependency/wave metadata. For example, `log.append("task.added", "D00", {"title": ..., "parent": "P1", "globs": [...]})` (and the same for `A0`, `F1`, `F2`, `R1`, `R2`, and the blocked `K*` tasks) has no `wave:N` tag and no `no-deps` tag for tasks with no prerequisites. This violates [r-task-phase-needs-wave], which says every task must state its dependencies in `needs` and carry a `wave:N` tag (or `no-deps` when it has no prerequisite).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_status_totals.py:36

chunk_findings.detail: `_data` now adds a `definition`/`totals` payload from `progress.queue_totals`, but it still computes `open_bugs` independently as `sum(1 for b in q.bugs() if b.open)`. The progress-line code explicitly excludes bugs with `resolution == "invalid"` before counting open bugs, and the new totals definition is intended to be the single bug source. Given a bug with `open=True` and `resolution="invalid"`, the STATUS.md export data can contain `open_bugs: 1` while the same export’s `definition`/`totals` (and the `Progress:` line) treat that bug as not a live/open bug, leaving two conflicting bug totals on the report path the change was meant to unify.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_status.py:63

chunk_findings.detail: Adding `"done"` to `TAIL_KEYS` makes the output cap keep the last entries of the `done` list by *list position* before the status renderer sees it. The renderer in `ddflow/surfaces/commands/reporting.py:_completed_lines` only then sorts `done` by `completed_at` and takes the newest rows, so the cap cannot be corrected after it has dropped rows. Given a capped status view with cap=1 and `done = [Task(id="B1", completed_at="2026-01-02"), Task(id="B2", completed_at="2026-01-01")]` (i.e. not already completion-ordered), the tail cap keeps `B2`; `_completed_lines` then prints `Completed (last 1 of 2):` and lists `B2`, even though the newest completion `B1` was discarded. The prose claims “newest completions” / “last N of TOTAL” but can show the wrong rows.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:TAIL_KEYS

chunk_findings.detail: The new `status_completed_shown` row says that when it is `0`, `allow_full = false` “does not govern” and the completed list stays “the whole completed set the row cap leaves.” The same table’s `allow_full` row says `allow_full = false` “stops 0 lifting a cap.” For a project with 20 completed tasks, `max_rows` default 50, `allow_full = false`, and `status_completed_shown = 0`, the new row documents showing all 20 completed tasks, while the `allow_full` row says the zero should not lift the cap and the answer should remain capped. This is a direct contract contradiction and lets an operator bypass the stated `allow_full` cap behavior.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/output-caps.md:25

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_fixture` creates tasks directly in the event log with payloads that contain only `title`, `parent`, `globs`, and sometimes `needs`; none of the task events carries a `wave` tag, and tasks with no prerequisites do not carry the required `no-deps` tag. The recorded project rule [r-task-phase-needs-wave] says every task must state its phase, dependencies in `needs`, and a `wave:N` tag (or `no-deps` when there are no prerequisites), so the tasks introduced by this change violate that guidance.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_status_totals.py:31-48

chunk_findings.detail: The regression guard `assert "12/" not in out.split("\n")[2]` is tied to an arbitrary output line rather than to the headline. If a regression leaves an old-style headline such as `Tasks: 12/5065 tasks complete` on the first status line but also emits the new definition phrase `15 of 19 live tasks done` later, the test can still pass: the phrase assertion succeeds and line index 2 may be a bucket line without `12/`. This lets the exact reported regression slip through the test that claims to guard it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_status_totals.py:66
